*PharmaCraft Daily - 09 Nov 2026*

🎓 *MBBS* (Renal & Diuretics)
Q: Furosemide acts on which part of the nephron?
Ans: Thick ascending limb of loop of Henle
Why: Loop diuretics inhibit the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter in the thick ascending limb; most potent diuretics.

🌍 *FMGE* (Renal & Diuretics)
Q: Which diuretic is used with a loop diuretic to treat resistant oedema (sequential blockade)?
Ans: Metolazone (thiazide-like)
Why: Metolazone added to a loop diuretic produces strong synergistic diuresis in resistant oedema.

🩺 *NEET PG* (Renal & Diuretics)
Q: Tolvaptan is also used to slow cyst growth in?
Ans: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
Why: Tolvaptan (V2 antagonist) slows progression in ADPKD; monitor for hepatotoxicity.

🏥 *INI-CET* (Renal & Diuretics)
Q: Why does chronic loop diuretic use cause metabolic alkalosis?
Ans: Contraction alkalosis with H+/K+ loss
Why: Loop diuretics cause volume contraction and increased distal H+/K+ secretion, producing metabolic alkalosis.

🔬 *MD Pharmacology* (Paper I: General/Experimental)
Q: Which isolated tissue preparation is classically used to study histamine responses?
Ans: Guinea pig ileum
Why: The guinea pig ileum is a classic preparation for histamine and acetylcholine dose-response studies.
